config.title: useDebounce

intro.title: useDebounce
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called useDebounce that delays the update of a value until after a specified wait time has passed without further changes. This is useful for optimizing performance by reducing the frequency of expensive operations, like API calls or state updates, triggered by rapid user input. You will learn to implement this using React's useState and useEffect hooks along with TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a reusable debounce hook that can be integrated into any React component to handle user interactions more efficiently.
intro.usecase: The useDebounce hook is essential for optimizing performance in search interfaces and data-heavy applications. You'll see it implemented in search bars on e-commerce sites like Amazon, where it prevents excessive API calls while users type queries. It's also crucial in dashboard filter controls that update charts and tables, ensuring smooth interactions without overwhelming the server. Additionally, form validation often uses debouncing to check username or email availability only after the user pauses typing.

objectives: Implement a custom useDebounce hook in TypeScript
Apply the useDebounce hook to control input field updates
Configure the debounce delay parameter for optimal performance
Initialize state variables to manage debounced values
Bind the useDebounce hook to form inputs in a React component
Render real-time and debounced values simultaneously in the UI
Integrate the useDebounce hook with API call simulations
